newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends at four-week low, funds sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends at four-week low, funds sell.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed a heavily-traded session just above four-week lows amid heavy fund liquidation, floor sources said.
The move sets the stage for additional losses, analysts said, pegging support in most-active July at 10.25 cents, a contract low hit on January 24.
"Sugar looks dim," Refco analyst Ann Prendergast, said.

She said talk of Russian buying coupled with fears of tight supplies fueled July to a contract high of 11.37 cents on April 23. Heavy deliveries deflated supply concerns, however, and sparked today's selloff.
"It's all over," Prendergast said. "The market is in for a major correction."
The most-active July contract ended down 0.26 cent to 10.70 cents per lb, having ranged from 10.86 to 10.67 cents. The back months settled 0.22 to 0.07 cent weaker.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 40,239 lots compared with Wednesday's official 25,512 lots.
Dealers expect the speculators to continue to liquidatie positionson Friday.
"With the big open interest, July will remain under pressure with the potential to fall to 10.25 to 10.50 cents," a floor source said, referring to open interest of 89,538 lots as of early Wednesday.
Some traders said the market could retrace today's losses to fill a gap on the charts basis July between 10.86 cents, where the contract opened, and 10.92 cents, the close on Wednesday.
The producers are likely to remain steady scale up sellers, however.
A weak close Wednesday and deliveries of 6,801 contracts today initiated early selling by the trade, which triggered stops below Friday's low of 10.91 cents and prompted fund liquidation.
July quickly plummeted to a three-week low of 10.72 cents, where short-covering by producers held the contract and lifted it to 10.84 cents at one point.
A second round of speculative liquidation just ahead of the close forced the most-active month to 10.67 cents, its weakest level since falling to 10.58 cents on April 1.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
